director.chapterArc: A tactical siege at Hallam Cross where a creature ambushes the group; Toren's training fails as stillness proves deceptive; Rook is mortally wounded holding a barrier while Senna and Wyck are injured. The scene shifts from high-intensity combat to clinical assessment of losses, ending with Rook revealing his inability to hold another gate.
director.restraintNote: Maintain the narrator's analytical distance during the creature description (P0031-P0048). Do not dramatize the violence; let the physical mechanics speak. The shift from combat to injury assessment must feel like a sudden, heavy silence. Rook's final lines are delivered with exhausted clarity, not melodrama.

cues.delivery: Clinical observation of the creature's unnatural construction; treat it as a physical anomaly rather than a monster.
cues.from: Later, when he had to describe it to people who wanted a description, Toren found that the only honest thing he could say was that it was the size of the cart and Pitch together, and that it was the colour of ash before it is ash, and that it was put together by somebody who had never been told what the parts were for.
cues.through: It came out of the dust at the fifth block low and fast with its head down. It had four limbs and they did not match. Three of them were legs — heavy, hooked, set wide, made for pushing. The fourth was a foreleg on the near side, and it was too long, and it was carried up and folded, and as it came it unfolded, and the whole length of it went flat and thin and hard and took an edge, and the edge came round at the height of a man's chest with the sound of a hand going through water.
cues.reason: Shift from narrative description to Toren's internal processing of the impossible.

cues.delivery: Rook's physical exertion and pain; a desperate, strained effort to hold the barrier.
cues.from: Rook had got there in the two seconds of the dust the only way left to him, which was on his hands and one knee across nine feet of grass, and he put his left hand flat down on the concrete apron at the foot of the sixth block and said something under his breath, and the air in front of the cart went hard.
cues.reason: Conveying Rook's sacrifice through vocal strain rather than shouting.

cues.delivery: Toren's catastrophic realization; the internal monologue should feel frantic but controlled.
cues.from: That's the wind-up, thought Toren, with absolute confidence, because a Verge-hound feints stillness before it commits and everybody who had ever survived one knew it, because Rook had told them so on a bridge in the fog in the first week and had made them say it back. A thing that goes still is a thing that is about to go.
cues.through: There was no gather. That was the whole of it and it was over before he understood any of it — the three driving legs did not crouch and did not load and did not do any of the things that a body does before a body moves; they were standing and then they were at full speed, and the thing went past him so close that the wind of it turned him round on his heel, and it was not in front of him any more, it was thirty feet behind him, at the gap between the fourth and the fifth block, which was the narrow one, and which had nothing but eleven feet of grass and the open behind it.
cues.reason: The moment of tactical failure and shock.

cues.delivery: Dessa's scream; a rare loss of composure that cuts through the tension.
cues.from: Dessa screamed his name. It was the only time in four months that Dessa Cole made a noise she had not decided to make.
cues.reason: The only time Dessa breaks her usual restraint.

cues.delivery: Dessa's analysis; flat, precise, and urgent. The realization that the training was inverted.
cues.from: "It drops one to pick up the other."
cues.through: Stillness is not disengagement. Stillness is the wind-up. A man had said that to five children on a bridge in the fog in the first week and made them say it back to him, and then: the side that goes quiet is the side that is coming. Always. Every time. It is the quiet flank, not the loud one. And a Stilt stops in the open because it has to stop to choose, and the stop is the only window anybody will ever get out of one. Every single thing in this country that had ever tried to kill them had taught the same lesson three different ways: watch the still part. The still part is where the next second comes from.
cues.reason: The critical tactical pivot where understanding shifts from wrong to right.

cues.delivery: Rook's command; urgent but grounded in the reality of his failing strength.
cues.from: "Yes," said Rook. "Now go and be right about it, because I can't hold that a second time and I'd rather you found out now than in nine minutes."
cues.through: Toren went out into the gap.
cues.reason: The final push before Toren acts on new understanding.

cues.delivery: Rook's dry observation about the ash; a moment of grim levity in exhaustion.
cues.from: Nobody laughed, and it had not quite been a joke, and it had been about a quarter of one.
cues.through: They took stock at dusk, because Rook made them, sitting in a row against the sixth block in the last of the wrong light.
cues.reason: The only humor in the chapter; delivered flatly to contrast with the horror.

cues.delivery: Rook's admission of his limits; a quiet, terrifying realization for Toren.
cues.from: Rook could not stand for more than about two minutes and could not shut a road again in less than three days, and said so, out loud, without being asked, which was the second time he had done that since the Level and which frightened Toren more than the morning had.
cues.through: "Right," said Rook. "Here's the arithmetic and I'm going to do all of it out loud, because I have spent eleven years doing it in my head and handing people the answer, and you're none of you children and the answer's bad.
cues.reason: The shift from physical injury to tactical impossibility.

cues.delivery: Rook's final instruction; exhausted but clear. The promise of a new path.
cues.from: Rook looked out at the flat dark country where four or five hundred pounds of ash was walking about on three legs.
cues.through: "You get some sleep," he said, "and in the morning I'm going to tell you the other thing."
cues.reason: The closing beat of the chapter.

pauses.reason: Major emotional landing: The creature's arrival and immediate threat established.
Emphasis on the narrator's constraint and Toren's limited perspective.

pauses.after: It dropped — the whole long flat weight of it came down off the horizontal and went loose at the shoulder, and it went quiet, and the edge came off it, and the end of it trailed in the grass.
pauses.reason: Scene turn: Toren realizes his training is wrong; a moment of shock before action resumes.
Critical misinterpretation; isolating the thought that drives Toren into danger.

pauses.after: Dessa screamed his name. It was the only time in four months that Dessa Cole made a noise she had not decided to make.
pauses.reason: Character reset: After the scream and immediate aftermath.

pauses.after: "The thing that goes quiet is the thing that isn't coming."
pauses.reason: Major revelation: The rule is stated; a long pause for Toren (and listener) to process the inversion of training.
Emphasis on the catastrophic nature of the realization.

pauses.after: And this one put down whatever it was not going to use.
pauses.reason: Completed thought: Transition from realization back to action.
The new tactical reality; isolating the key descriptors for Toren's focus.

pauses.after: He rolled. He got up. His hand was empty and his palm was opened across the base of the fingers where the spike had gone out of it sideways and he did not notice that for another quarter of an hour.
pauses.reason: Scene turn: The creature's failure and retreat; a moment of stunned silence before the aftermath begins.

pauses.after: "Then we'll all lie down," said Rook, "in a concrete pen, four miles from a wall, with a Barrel on the flat that has learned this morning that we can hurt it. Have you ever sold ash?"
pauses.reason: Completed thought: Rook's grim assessment of their situation.
Introducing a new term; isolating the definition for clarity.

pauses.after: Rook could not stand for more than about two minutes and could not shut a road again in less than three days, and said so, out loud, without being asked, which was the second time he had done that since the Level and which frightened Toren more than the morning had.
pauses.reason: Character reset: The admission of inability to hold the road again; a heavy beat for Toren.
Emphasis on Toren's success despite his injuries and fear.
